second_scan_confirmations.what: Readings settled by finding each entry's own symptom sentences in a SECOND SCAN of the same book (Internet Archive item in.ernet.dli.2015.94901, Bell, Homoeopathic Therapeutics, 7th ed. 1906). The remedy heading above the matched sentences is the entry's remedy; the line number is the evidence.

readings.evidence: 'Drowsiness with chilliness' sits at line 910, inside section 4 'JETIIUSA CYMPItM' (between ACONITE and AGARICUS). Not Jatropha and not Justicia.
'Chilliness when leaving the fire' at line 1070, inside '6. ALOE'.
'Chilliness along the spine, followed by hot flashes and sweat' at line 2246, inside '24. BOLETUS LARICIS'. Yes - Boletus is a remedy in this book and the symptom is its own.

'Chilliness in the rectum' at line 5786, inside '88. LYCOPODIUM'.
'Chilliness over the head and legs' at line 1995, inside '20. BARYTA CARBOYICA'.
'Want of animal heat, always chilly, even when exercising' at line 8132, inside the Silicea section between SEPIA and STANNUM (the scan prints 'Silic.' and 'Silicea.' there).
'Chilliness and sensitiveness to cold' in the 'SIBADlLLi' (Sabadilla) section.

not_a_remedy.evidence: all three of its 'sentences' are fragments of the book's own repertory index ('Sulph. Chilly persons, in: Asar. E.', line 10019) - a page of cross-references, not a remedy. Withheld rather than named.
